headline.caveat: up to 160M AMD shares at $0.01 strike (~10% of AMD fully vested); vests in tranches tied to OpenAI's GPU-deployment milestones and AMD stock-price targets (up to $600/share for the final tranche)

realized_to_date.caveat: no tranches vested; zero financial-statement impact through AMD FY2025 per the 10-K/A, as no vesting conditions have been met

nature_md: Issued Oct 6, 2025 concurrently with the 6GW GPU purchase agreement: OpenAI may purchase up to 160M AMD shares at $0.01 each, vesting in tranches as (a) OpenAI hits Instinct GPU purchase/deployment milestones (first tranche at the first 1GW) and (b) AMD's stock reaches specified price targets. Essentially penny-priced equity handed to the customer as an inducement to buy — economically a rebate paid in stock. AMD's amended FY2025 annual report (10-K/A, Feb 2026) confirms the accounting: consideration payable to a customer, to be recognized as **contra-revenue** (reducing reported revenue) as vesting becomes probable — with zero impact so far because nothing has vested.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Consideration payable to a customer under ASC 606: the warrant's fair value will be recorded as contra-revenue (a reduction of the revenue from OpenAI GPU sales) as tranches become probable of vesting. Through FY2025: no financial-statement impact. If fully vested, AMD hands over ~10% of the company; dilution hits shareholders rather than the income statement's cash costs.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: OpenAI holds an option-like asset costing effectively nothing, worth tens of billions if it deploys the 6GW and AMD's stock performs — its GPU purchases are partially self-funding via supplier equity. Any gain is investment income, unrelated to OpenAI's operating economics.

both_sides_md: **Bear:** paying your customer ~10% of your company to buy your product is demand manufactured with equity — and because the cost lands as contra-revenue only later, near-term reported revenue from the deal overstates its true economics (the Chanos vendor-financing critique in warrant form). **Bull:** the structure is cash-free, costs AMD nothing unless OpenAI actually deploys 6GW *and* AMD shareholders enjoy large price appreciation — a self-funding customer-acquisition tool for the #2 GPU vendor breaking an effective monopoly (AMD's own framing; deal disclosed transparently in SEC filings).

events.title: AMD 10-K/A details warrant accounting: contra-revenue, no impact yet
events.why_it_matters: Establishes the audited treatment — the clearest on-the-record example of warrant-for-revenue accounting in the AI cycle.
